description: One person's access to the Farm Ops mobile app: which role they hold, which entities they may see, when their API token was issued and when — and by whom, and why — it was taken away. Frappe's User, Has Role and User Permission tables hold the access itself; this holds the story around it, which is the part an audit asks for and the part Frappe keeps nowhere.
name: Mobile Access Grant

fields.description: The Frappe User this grant is about. One grant per user: re-issuing a token updates this row rather than adding a second one, so there is exactly one place to look for 'what does this person have'.
fields.label: User

fields.description: Their name as it should read on a phone's account screen.
fields.label: Full Name

fields.description: Which of the six mobile roles this account was made for: Field Worker, Foreman, Compliance Officer, Farm Manager, Family Member or Advisor. The authority on what they may actually do is the Has Role table; this records what the account was FOR, which is the question 'why does this person have a login' asks.
fields.label: Mobile Role

fields.description: Active means the account is enabled and its token has not been revoked. Expired means the review date on the token has passed and nobody has acted on it — Frappe API secrets do not expire on their own, so this is a flag for a human, not an enforcement. Revoked means somebody took it away, and revocation_reason says why.
fields.label: State

fields.description: Which entity the app should open on. One of the companies in entity_access, and the one carrying is_default on this user's Company User Permission.
fields.label: Preferred Company

fields.description: The Companies this account was granted, one per line. THE AUTHORITY IS THE User Permission TABLE, not this field — this is the record of what was asked for, so a grant that drifted from its User Permissions is visible rather than silent. list_mobile_users reports both and names the difference.
fields.label: Entity Access

fields.description: The public half of the Frappe API credential — the part before the colon in 'Authorization: token <api_key>:<api_secret>'. Recorded so an operator reading an access log can tell whose key it was. THE SECRET IS NOT HERE AND IS NOT ANYWHERE THIS APP CAN READ IT: Frappe stores it encrypted in its own password table, and generate_api_token is the only moment it exists in plaintext.
fields.label: API Key

fields.description: When the current token was generated.
fields.label: Token Issued On

fields.description: The date the token should be reviewed and re-issued. A REVIEW DATE, NOT AN EXPIRY: Frappe API secrets have no expiry of their own. From v0.17.1 there IS a scheduled sweep, but it works on IDLENESS (last_seen_on) rather than on this date — a credential in daily use is not stale because a review date passed, and one nobody has touched for a month is stale whatever this says. list_mobile_users flags a grant past this date loudly; revoke_api_token is what ends it on demand.
fields.label: Token Review Due

fields.description: When the token was invalidated. Set by revoke_api_token and by revoke_mobile_user.
fields.label: Token Revoked On

fields.description: How many times a token has been issued for this account. A number climbing on one account is somebody losing a phone repeatedly, which is a fact worth being able to see.
fields.label: Tokens Issued

fields.description: The last time this credential actually made a call, stamped by the mobile API gate at most once a day. EMPTY MEANS IT HAS NEVER BEEN USED — a card that was printed and never scanned reads the same as one scanned this morning if you only look at token_issued_on, and those are very different facts about a live credential.
fields.label: Last Seen On

fields.description: Exempt this grant from the idle sweep. Tick it for a credential that is legitimately quiet for months — a winter caretaker, a device kept for a seasonal crew, an integration. Everything else has its token revoked after the idle window on ERPNext MCP Settings, which is what limits the blast radius of a phone lost in an orchard and never reported. The ACCOUNT is never disabled by the sweep; only the token goes.
fields.label: Exempt From Idle Sweep
Devices
fields.description: Every phone that holds, held or was offered a credential on this account. v0.175.0: phones authenticate against these rows and nothing else.

fields.label: Devices
fields.description: Written by the enrolment flow, never by hand: a credential is minted by the server when a phone exchanges its one-time QR token. Revoke one device with revoke_mobile_device or the Revoke Device button; the others keep working.
When a login QR was last produced for this account.
fields.label: Last QR Issued

fields.description: When the QR payload stops being valid to enrol with. Short by design — the QR carries a live credential in a form anybody can photograph over somebody's shoulder, so it is minted for the length of an onboarding conversation and not for the length of a season.
fields.label: QR Expires At

fields.description: The Governance Document the QR was filed against, where one was asked for. That is the offline distribution path: a camp office with no signal prints the archived copy.
fields.label: QR Archive Document

fields.description: The public HTTPS base URL the QR pointed the app at — the Tailscale Funnel address, normally. Recorded because an account enrolled against a URL that has since changed is an account that stops working for a reason nobody can see from the phone.
fields.label: Endpoint URL

fields.description: Who took it away.
fields.label: Revoked By

fields.description: Why. REQUIRED WHEN state IS Revoked, and the controller refuses without it. 'Left at the end of harvest', 'phone lost in the orchard', 'moved to the packing house' and 'dismissed for cause' are four different answers to an auditor's question about why somebody's access ended, and a blank field answers none of them.
fields.label: Revocation Reason

fields.description: Anything else about this account somebody will want in six months.
fields.label: Notes
